About Us / Disclaimer: 

Police Insider provides unbiased and authentic footage of incidents captured on body cams. We believe this footage can be used as an educational guide for viewers. 

We only provide unique and original content that hasn’t been covered before on YouTube.

The raw footage for the videos on this channel have been obtained directly from the respective Police Departments. We as a media company have the right to use it commercially. Most incidents may require a fee associated with the request and take several days to process.

The channel is not affiliated with any law enforcement agency.

Our channel is compliant with YouTube's Fair Use Policy as we create a storyline and cut down several hours of long footage to a few minutes to bring out the most entertaining and educational parts, just like other channels such as Code Blue Cam, Real World Police, Active Police Cam, Blue Watch and Bodycam FIles.

The featured content is NOT intended to publicly shame, ridicule, or degrade the individuals involved or to glorify violence in any way.

While Officer Metz and Dallas were lucky enough not to sustain life-threatening gunshot wounds, 35-year-old Jeffrey, on the other hand, had multiple bullet wounds all over his body. all over his body. He had to be airlifted that night as his condition worsened. Following the incident seven officers, including Officer Mets, were placed on paid administrative leave until the investigation concluded. However, this wasn't Jeffrey's first rodeo, as he had already served nearly four years in prison for a high-speed pursuit in 2021, which he admitted he initiated because he was attempting suicide by cop. He was released in January 2025, just nine months months before shooting officer Mets. 35-year-old Emerson Jeffrey was arraigned on the new charges that came down last week from a special Allen County grand jury. Jeffrey is facing four counts of felonious assault with specifications of shooting at police officers and shooting from a vehicle. He's also facing charges of discharging a gun over the roadway and other gun related charges. If Jeffrey is convicted on all of those charges and gets the maximum sentences, he is facing over 120 years in prison. Jeffrey's bond is set at $2.5 million, and he's currently in the Allen County Jail after being released from the hospital about two weeks after the incident. Officer Mets in Dallas were discharged after treatment, while Jeffrey's next trial is scheduled for April 27, 2026. Six out of the seven officers who were placed on administrative leave were later called back and assigned non-enforcement roles. Officer Mets is still recovering from the gunshot wounds.
